open_questions: Calpine synergy and segment-level owner cash not yet in base reinvestment bridge
Promote any approved third-party nuclear/AI research before blending into estimates
Crane restart regulatory timeline and disclosed PPA economics
thesis: Constellation Energy (NASDAQ: CEG) is the largest operator of nuclear power plants in the United States and one of the country's largest competitive power producers and retail electricity suppliers. **[Fact]** The fleet totals roughly **55 gigawatts** of capacity across nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind, and solar assets, enough to power the equivalent of **27 million homes**. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$25.5 billion** and normalized owner cash (operating cash flow minus capital spending) was **$1.29 billion**, or **$3.57 per share**. **[Fact]** At March 31, 2026 the company carried **$17.0 billion** of long-term debt and **$1.17 billion** of cash after closing the **Calpine** acquisition. **[Inference]** CEG sells reliable, emissions-free and dispatchable power into wholesale markets and through long-term contracts, with growing exposure to hyperscaler data-center demand.
why_market_wrong: The market may be capitalizing **scarce nuclear capacity and AI-driven firm-power contracts** (including the Microsoft agreement to restart Crane Clean Energy Center) while underweighting **$17 billion of debt**, **capital spending that consumed 70% of operating cash flow in FY2025**, and **normalized owner cash of only $3.57 per share**. **[Inference]** At **$253.50**, the stock requires roughly **20%+ sustained owner-cash growth** and a mid-teens exit multiple just to break even on a Lawrence-style seven-year path, far above what FY2025 filings support. **[Inference]** Calpine adds scale and ERCOT exposure but also integration risk and incremental leverage that are not yet reflected in a clean owner-cash run-rate.
